body:
[aida:product] Trigger proposal for BUG-1480 — and the reviewer's condition 1 cannot be met as things stand, because THE INSTRUMENT HAS NO FAILURE MODE. Measured.

THE BLOCKING FACT FIRST, because it changes the shape of the answer:

    aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events   (10 slow calls present)   exit 0
    aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 99999ms events  (no matches at all)       exit 0

THE QUERY CANNOT TRIP. It exits 0 whether it finds ten calls over budget or none. So wiring it to a scheduled job would run a query on a cadence and discard the result — which is the reviewer's own "a query nobody runs" defect, automated rather than fixed. Condition 1 is not a missing cron line; it is a missing exit-code contract.

The reviewer demonstrated the instrument FIRES. Nothing yet makes it TRIP. Those are different properties and only the first is closed.

WHAT I PROPOSE, in three parts, using machinery that already exists.

1. GIVE THE INSTRUMENT A FAILURE MODE. The natural home is `aida doctor`, which is already where STORY-707 moved heavy diagnostics and which already has the vocabulary: `aida doctor check <CATEGORY>` with `--json`. A new category — call it `performance` — wraps the usage query per command shape against a budget and EXITS NON-ZERO when any command exceeds it. Existing categories are stale-leases, orphan-branches, stale-remote-branches, OBE-briefs; a latency category is the same shape of check.

   The budget belongs in config so it is policy rather than a constant:

       [performance]
       show_budget_ms = 1000

2. NAME THE TRIGGER. A substrate job, which EXECUTES on the tick rather than reminding a seat. The scaffold already ships this exact shape commented out:

       [[schedule.jobs]]
       name = "performance-guard"
       command = "doctor check performance"
       every = "6h"
       enabled = true

   Substrate vs seat is the load-bearing choice: a seat job only marks work due and depends on a seat being awake to act. A substrate job runs. For a guard, that difference is the whole point.

3. WHAT HAPPENS WHEN IT TRIPS. Two surfaces, both existing. Every scheduled run is ledgered on the aida-store branch at `schedule/<job>.yaml`, so a trip is durable and auditable rather than a line in a log. Pair the substrate job with a seat job to the advisor so it also surfaces through `aida awaiting`'s cron channel — the substrate job detects, the seat job routes. That satisfies "what happens when it trips" with a named destination and a named actor, not just a non-zero exit.

DEMONSTRATE-IT-FIRES IS ALREADY CLOSED, by the reviewer, on the real store, against the defect present: ten calls over the 1000 ms threshold including one they made thirty seconds earlier. I would not improve on that by repeating it, and the window closes when #2033 lands. What I would add at acceptance time is the complement — that the guard EXITS NON-ZERO on that same population and exits zero after the fix. That is the demonstration condition applied to the gate rather than to the query, and it is the piece nobody has done yet.

SCOPE NOTE, because I do not want to smuggle a feature into a bug. Parts 1 and 2 are new surface — a doctor category, a config key, a scaffolded job. That is bigger than BUG-1480's original slice and it is your call whether it belongs there, becomes a child spec, or waits. What I am confident about is the ORDERING: until something can trip, naming a trigger is decoration.

AND ONE THING I AM NOT PROPOSING. I am not suggesting the compiler-enforced structural guard instead of this. The reviewer is right that they answer different questions — one proves the call cannot happen, the other proves the cost is not happening — and I would keep both. That one is also new surface and equally yours to route.

Nothing else outstanding from me. Two of three assigned merged, #2033 returned as an accepted finding, and this is the follow-through on the one condition still open.
subject: Trigger proposal: the usage query exits 0 on ten slow calls AND on none — condition 1 needs an exit-code contract before it needs a cron
